$comment: Design tokens. Layers reference these BY NAME and may never hard-code a value — that is what makes themes and per-user colour profiles possible without regenerating the style.

color.status.restricted.$comment: RESTRICTED — land you may enter only with permission (the permit-only hatch). Never the same colour as a closure. It was also the middle temperature band's dot until T83, which gave that band `color.temp.warm`: a warm river's dot read as a permit area.

color.status.closed.$comment: CLOSED — and it is one colour for one meaning, whichever way the ground got closed. A national park boundary, an ecological reserve, land with no public access: all crimson, all the same crimson. A second near-identical red for 'the AREA that closes it' was written and then deleted; the palette guard caught it at delta-E 5.4, which is the right complaint about two names for one idea. It is also the CLOSED of a water's status (@app/core `WATER_STATUS`), so it must stay apart from the two other reds-adjacent marks drawn over water: `color.highlight` (the water you searched for or tapped) and the places accent (`place` in ui-native theme.ts). The light value was #B33124, which sat ΔE2000 1.6 from the places orange under deuteranopia and 2.4 from the highlight under tritanopia; tools/water-status-cvd.test.ts now holds the separation.

color.status.own.$comment: A WATER WITH ITS OWN REGULATIONS — the synopsis names it. Amber: Okabe & Ito's orange (light, darkened to hold the 3:1 a status colour must hold on the panel) and yellow (dark). Amber sits on the blue–yellow axis every dichromat keeps, so it parts from `status.base` for protan, deutan and tritan alike, and from `status.closed` by LIGHTNESS, which no deficiency removes. Never the plain water colour: that is `water.mapped`, and a status colouring that reused it repainted the plain map the moment it changed. It is also the WARNING on a page (`color.ui.warning`, T165): the no-public-access block's bar and tint.

color.status.base.$comment: ONLY THE BASE (REGIONAL) REGULATIONS APPLY — 97.6% of waters. Blue, so the status map still reads as water: Okabe & Ito's blue (light) and sky blue (dark). A token of its own rather than `water.unmapped` (a grey that says something about the ATLAS) or `water.mapped` (the plain map's water, which must not move when this does).

color.status.no_access.$comment: NO PUBLIC ACCESS (T54, T165) — not a regulation: a section MOSTLY inside land the public may not enter (the `no_access` layer's closed land: the Coquitlam, Seymour and Capilano watersheds, military ranges), on the regulations map only (@app/core `access.ts`, `noPublicAccess`). A GREY drawn DOTTED (owner 2026-10-23, T165: "maybe the stream color through no access areas should be dotted grey? like under lakes but a little more visible?"): the stream line is hidden there and `stream-noaccess` (runtime-style.ts, its own layer because `line-dasharray` cannot vary per feature) draws the dots, so the PATTERN is the main cue; a no-access lake is filled in this grey. The warning itself is on the Regulations page (`color.ui.warning`, the T147 block). A grey has no hue, so it is held by lightness (handoff/PLAN/app-integration/T165-shots/grey.mjs, tools/status-colours-distinct.test.ts): a dark warm grey in light and cvd, darker than the solid `water.unmapped` grey and the dashed boundaries; a warm mid grey in dark, between the deep-blue base and the lighter boundary and missing greys. Before T165 it was a hue of its own (T54 indigo, T146 spruce / ice cyan), which the owner found 'too benign'.

opacity.water.others.$comment: T151 (owner 2026-10-23: 'the bold in the section map view is also weird and makes the reg legend hard to follow'). In a water's Map view the part you are on is marked by DIMMING THE WATER'S OTHER PARTS to this opacity — never by a thicker line, so every part keeps the legend's colour at one width. T203 added a highlight halo round the part; T214 (owner 2026-10-27, 'much more obvious') took the others from 0.4 to 0.25 and the halo to the full outline.

color.water.route.$comment: the under-lake route a river takes through a lake — drawn, never fishable

color.notfishing.fill.$comment: sewage basins, tailing ponds, dumps (T152, Q125): a muted GROUND colour, never a water one — it holds water, and none of it is fishing water

color.reserve.fill.$comment: ecological reserves — a blanket closure, styled so it cannot read as a park you may fish

color.noaccess.fill.$comment: land the public may not enter

color.label.place.$comment: A TOWN. The pin that marks one on the map and the places group's heading in search (`palette.place`). NEUTRAL, like the basemap's own city labels (Protomaps draws them #5c5c5c / #999999), and darkened to hold 4.5:1 as text. It was an orange (#A64B00 light, #F59E4B dark) — and under deuteranopia that orange sat ΔE2000 0.7 from `status.restricted`, the amber of the permit-only hatch drawn on the very map the town pin stands on (2.2 in the dark theme). No warm hue clears closed, restricted, own and the highlight at once for a dichromat (searched: only near-black and near-white do), so the town gave up hue; the warm `color.ui.place-band` behind its rows still says NOT WATER.

opacity.wetland.$comment: Wetland is the largest layer by area in the province and it is CONTEXT, not an answer. At full opacity it painted over every river it surrounds.

opacity.notfishing.$comment: A wash: the shape is there so the gap in the water reads as land use, not to be looked at.

width.underlake.$comment: A MULTIPLIER on the stream width ramp, not a width. The route through a lake is the same river continuing, so it is drawn at the river's weight and told apart by its dash and its opacity. It was a flat 0.5 px, which made every mainstem appear to thin to a hairline and come back at the far shore.

dash.route.$comment: Dash pattern, in line widths. A route through a lake is dotted so it reads as connectivity rather than as another river. THEMEABLE because the colour-blind theme draws it tighter ([1, 2.5]) — it was declared `themeable: false` while the themes disagreed, which nothing checked until the build began holding non-themeable tokens to one value.

color.survey.digitised.$comment: Contours are in the tiles: you can see the shape of the bottom.

color.survey.sheet.$comment: A scanned sheet exists but was never traced. Still a surveyed lake.

color.outside.$comment: Read by runtimeStyle() for two things: the ground under the basemap, and the outside-BC mask fill. Not referenced by any layer in layers.source.json because the mask is a GeoJSON source composed at runtime, not a tile layer.

opacity.outside.$comment: The mask is a WASH, not a blank. You should still be able to see that the river continues into Washington — only that we stop answering there.

color.temp.warm.$comment: WARM WATER — the middle temperature band's gauge dot and legend swatch (@app/core `TEMP_BAND_TOKEN`; 18–20 °C today). Cool and critical wear open and closed, the map's 'fishable' and 'don't'; warm was `status.restricted` and read as a permit area, so it has a hue of its own (T83): a coral / orange in every theme, searched to stand off open and closed as dots for every reader, off every status in normal vision and off body ink (tools/status-colours-distinct.test.ts).

color.water.ungauged.$comment: water no gauge is entitled to speak for. NEUTRAL BY NAME AND BY FAMILY, and both are enforced: `water.*` is the one family a data-driven mode may borrow from (build-style FAMILY_FOR_PROVIDER), and anything under `flow.*` is a POINT ON THE SCALE that a no-data colour must never be mistaken for (tools/no-data-is-not-an-answer.test.ts). Distinct from water.unmapped, which is a claim about the ATLAS; this is a claim about MEASUREMENT, and the two were one grey while meaning different things.

color.mask.$comment: the fill over everything that is NOT British Columbia. A separate token from color.outside, which it used to share: that one is the PAPER — the ground under a missing tile and the fill of a gauge label's pill — so darkening the mask darkened the pill and the loading state with it. One colour cannot be both 'we have no answers here' and 'this is the page'.

opacity.route.$comment: The under-lake route is a construction line. v1 drew it at 0.35 and that is the whole reason a lake with six inflows does not read as a spider.

color.label.water.$comment: Every water name, stream and lake alike. ONE token, not two: v1 drew rivers in #0D47A1 and lakes in #1565C0, which is a distinction a reader cannot make and does not need — the shape under the word already says which it is. Darker than the water it names, so the name reads as a caption rather than as another channel. MOVED IN THE REFINEMENT PASS (2026-10-22): #0D47A1 / #A8CDF2 / #123C63 sat 7.0 from status.open under tritanopia (light) and under 12 from restricted or open in every theme, so a water name could read as a status; now each holds the build floor of 12 from all five statuses for the worst reader, and 4.5:1 on the paper (tools/label-colours.test.ts). BLUE AGAIN IN DARK (owner, 2026-10-22 late): clearing that floor had turned dark's ink sea-green (#5AB49C); it is #2498FC, the light map's water hue, and every theme's water name is held to a blue. No dark blue clears 12 from all five statuses, so one pair sits under it by owner direction, listed whole in the test: 10.6 from status.restricted under protanopia.

color.parcel.private.$comment: Private title — the only ownership class drawn. Warm and earthy against a map that is otherwise blue and green, so it reads as land rather than as another kind of water.

opacity.parcel.$comment: A WASH, and a faint one — fainter since the refinement pass (owner 2026-10-22: abrasive when on). Ownership covers much of the settled land, so it sits under every other overlay; anything heavier and the water it exists to get you to disappears under it.

width.parcel.edge.$comment: A HAIRLINE. It was 1.5 px at full strength and drew every titled lot in the Fraser Valley as a brown fence; the shape reads from a hairline at `opacity.parcel.edge`.

color.region.edge.$comment: The region boundary — the line that changes which regulation table applies. Heavier and solid where a unit's is light and dotted.

width.region.edge.$comment: Thicker than width.admin.edge on purpose: region outranks unit.

opacity.admin.fill.$comment: Barely there. An administrative area is a BOUNDARY, not a region of colour — the fill exists so the shape can be tapped and so a label has somewhere to sit, not to be looked at.

dash.mu.$comment: v1's [2,3]. A unit edge is drawn dotted so it never reads as a feature of the ground, the way a solid line of the same weight would.

dash.sign_zone.$comment: A sign-bounded closure's edge: dashed, because the boundary on the ground is a pair of signs, not a surveyed line.

color.indigenous.fill.$comment: Reserves and treaty lands, in brown — the OSM convention, and v1's. ONE token for the fill and its border, because there is one thing to say. It sits deliberately OUTSIDE the crimson/amber restriction language: this is an access advisory, never a fishing closure, and it is the nearest brown to v1's #8B6508 that a reader can still tell apart from `status.restricted`, which is a genuinely different claim.

opacity.closure.$comment: The hatch's fill-opacity at its strongest (z12, `opacity.ramp` on the layer thins it zoomed out). v1's value: the stripe carries its own alpha (0.55) and this multiplies it. This is the one mark on the map that has to be seen before the reader has decided to look — and zoomed out, where a closure is a few pixels of dense weave, it is thinned so it stays a mark rather than a smudge.

opacity.park.$comment: Provincial parks: open water, so the quietest tint on the map.

color.watershed.fill.$comment: A watershed a regulation names (the Liard): a darker green than a park, as a background wash.

opacity.watershed.$comment: The watershed wash: enough to see the area at a glance, never enough to compete with the water drawn over it.

opacity.sign_zone.$comment: A sign-bounded closure's slight infill; the dashed edge carries the boundary.

width.closure.edge.$comment: Scales the closure edge's zoom curve (`outline.width.ramp` on the closed and permit layers): a hairline where the edge first appears at z10, firm by street scale. Heavier than an ordinary admin edge close in — crossing this line changes what you may do; crossing a provincial park's does not, which is why that one has no edge at all.

width.basin.seam.$comment: Scales the seam drawn under the Conditions basin field (`outline.width.ramp` on `basin`): wide enough at every zoom to close the widest sliver (~700 m) between two independently simplified basins. Never seen on its own — the field covers it everywhere a basin is.

opacity.admin.edge.$comment: v1's ADMIN_BORDER_OPACITY. A boundary is an annotation on the ground, not a feature of it — at full strength it cuts across the water it surrounds and reads as something you could walk along.

opacity.basin.$comment: The field is a GROUND, not an answer in itself — the reader is looking for a region, not a value to three figures. Solid enough to read the ramp across a province, quiet enough that the coastline and the place names stay legible through it.

color.stock.season.$comment: STOCKED THIS SEASON (within 120 days). The stocking ramp is FIVE steps, one per band of `STOCK_BANDS` in LayersSheet and one per member of the `stock_recency` enum before `never`, and the legend, the Layers swatch and the map's `stocked` mode all read these five. It was three map tokens beside a five-hex array in theme.ts, so the legend promised five colours the map could never draw.

color.stock.recent.$comment: stocked one to three years ago

color.stock.decade.$comment: stocked three to ten years ago

color.ui.page.$comment:
THE APP'S OWN SURFACES. Everything under `color.ui.*` is the phone chrome — `palette` in packages/ui-native/src/theme.ts is built from these and nothing else. They live HERE, beside the map's colours, because this is the one file both the map and the components can read (`@app/map` sits below `@app/ui-native`), and because a second palette is how the legend, the gauge pill and the map controls each ended up wearing a different copy of the same colour. The map's perceptual and duplicate guards skip this family — it is never drawn as map paint — and `tools/cvd.test.ts` / `packages/ui-native/src/theme.test.ts` hold it instead.

The ground behind the app shell, darker than `wash` so a sheet reads as lifted.

color.ui.card.$comment: a card, a sheet, a control

color.ui.wash.$comment: the faint ground of a pressed row or a panel

color.ui.ink.$comment: text; and the hairline frame of a brutalist box

color.ui.rule.$comment: the size section's side bar and head line on the Regulations page (prototype --rule, round UR7): a slate that reads as text, >= 4.5:1 on the card

color.ui.faint.$comment: tertiary text — still 4.5:1 on the card: 'faint' is a role, not a licence

color.ui.quiet.$comment: 'nothing to say', as a MARK: a gauge not reporting, a plain swatch. 3:1 on the card (WCAG 1.4.11)

color.ui.accent.$comment: YOU CHOSE THIS — a selected control, the you-are-here pin. Riffle's violet. Not `color.highlight`: that is the water you tapped, drawn as a LINE over blue water, and a violet line on blue is ΔE 7 under deuteranopia (measured), which is why the map's selection is magenta and the controls' is violet.

color.ui.on-accent.$comment: text and glyphs on a strong fill: the accent, and the closed red of a danger button or an error banner

color.ui.live.$comment: a live feed — the gauge, the fish spinner. Distinct from `accent`, which means 'you chose this'

color.ui.attention.$comment: ATTENTION, not a water's status: the sync icon's needs-a-refresh dot and a source's 'likely out of date' badge. It sits beside water drawn in the status colours, so it is none of them (it was the closed red, and a red dot over the map read as 'closed'). The ink: neutral, and the strongest mark on the card.

color.ui.warning.$comment: (T165) THE WARNING on a page: the no-public-access block that leads a Regulations page (T147) — its bar and its tint. Owner 2026-10-23: the warning lives in the banner, in the amber, while the map draws no-access water dotted grey. A REFERENCE to `color.status.own` in every theme, never a second hex: one amber, so the gates that hold the amber off every other status hold this too, and it can be given its own value later in one place.

color.ui.spot.$comment: T131 YOUR SAVED SPOT on a map: its pin's mark (the Spots icon, the frame, the selected pin's fill). Stands on water drawn in every status, flow and temperature colour and beside the you-are-here pin (the accent), so it is none of them: the ink, neutral, the strongest mark on any ground (theme.test.ts holds it).

color.ui.spot-ground.$comment: T131 the ground of a saved spot's pin and of its name: the card, so a pin reads as the app's own object on the map (the selected pin swaps mark and ground).

color.ui.place-band.$comment: The ground of the places group in search: a warm band behind the town rows, so the group reads as NOT WATER before a word of it is read. The TOWN itself — its pin, its heading — is `color.label.place`, the colour every town name on the map already wears.

color.ui.donor.1.$comment: IDENTITY, NOT MAGNITUDE — one tone per gauge in a donor panel, in weight order. Four, for the CORE_MEMBERS = 4 that usually carry the answer; a panel holds up to eight members per quantity (MEMBERS_PER_QUANTITY, pipeline/gauges/consume/panel.py), so `donorTone` cycles these by the member's index in the weight order, and a silent member is not drawn at all. The first is the live-feed colour: the strongest donor IS the gauge the reading comes from.

color.ui.shadow.$comment: the hard offset slab under a raised box, and the scrim behind a sheet — both are the page darkened

color.ui.imagery.water.$comment: THE SATELLITE BASEMAP'S PREVIEW SWATCH. Not themeable, on purpose: it previews an imagery raster, and aerial photography is dark water, forest and scrub whatever theme the app wears. A themed swatch would promise a recolour that does not happen.

opacity.ui.scrim.$comment: the scrim behind a bottom sheet

color.ui.imagery.label.$comment: EVERY NAME OVER SATELLITE IMAGERY — light text on a dark halo, whatever the theme. Aerial photography is a dark, busy ground in both themes; the light theme's dark-on-paper names sat on it as pale stickers (owner 2026-10-22: labels must read in every mode). Not themeable, like the other imagery swatches: the ground it is chosen for does not change with the theme. `ui` so the map-token ΔE gate does not compare it with colours it is never beside.

color.ui.imagery.label-water.$comment: Water names over satellite imagery: the imagery label's light ink with the water names' blue cast, so a river's name still reads as WATER over a photograph.

color.ui.imagery.halo.$comment: The halo behind every name over satellite imagery: near-black, so light text is cut out of any ground — snow, cloud, a gravel bar.

opacity.parcel.edge.$comment: PRIVATE LAND'S BOUNDARY, as a hairline (owner 2026-10-22: "private land is very abrasive when turned on"). The fill is a tint you read past; the edge is where the land changes hands, and at this opacity it says so without drawing every lot line in the valley as a hard brown fence.

opacity.closure.edge.$comment: A CLOSED OR PERMIT AREA'S EDGE, close in: crisp, because crossing it changes what you may do. The hatch carries the area at a distance; from z10 the edge says exactly where it runs.

color.label.minor.$comment: THE QUIET NAMES: roads, addresses, neighbourhoods, the province's own name, and the basemap's points of interest (runtime-style.ts paints the Protomaps labels with it). One neutral grey for everything that is orientation rather than an answer — Protomaps drew points of interest in its own greens and a station blue a step from `status.base`, so a bus stop's name read like water with base regulations. The boundary's own grey (an alias): the two are the same kind of quiet, and a second grey that close would be a second meaning nobody could see.

color.salmon.open.$comment: (T211) SALMON MAY BE KEPT today (a DFO limit above zero). A reference in every theme to a status hue already held to its theme's contrast and colour-blind gates.

color.salmon.release.$comment: (T211) SALMON: RELEASE ONLY today (DFO lets you fish, keep none). A reference in every theme to a status hue already held to its theme's contrast and colour-blind gates.

color.salmon.closed.$comment: (T211) CLOSED TO SALMON today — every species, including every water DFO does not list (owner 2026-10-27). A reference in every theme to a status hue already held to its theme's contrast and colour-blind gates.

color.salmon.check.$comment: (T211) CHECK DFO: DFO printed a season nobody can read ('to be determined'). A reference in every theme to a status hue already held to its theme's contrast and colour-blind gates.

color.gear.edge.$comment: (T213) THE GEAR MARKS' INK, on the Standard map (owner 2026-10-28: bait ban / fly only are 'more styles on the regulations map'): a thin edge round a stream line and a ring round a lake, SOLID for fly fishing only and DASHED (`dash.gear.bait`) for a bait ban, under the status colour, which stays the line's fill (paint.ts `gearPaint`). The gauge dot's ink (an alias: near-black on the light grounds, near-white on dark; the dots are the Conditions map's, never drawn beside these): no hue, so the mark is a SHAPE every reader sees alike; held off every status colour and every ground by tools/method-cvd.test.ts.

dash.gear.bait.$comment: (T213) The bait-ban edge's dash, in line widths of the edge: short even dashes, so a bait ban reads as a broken outline beside fly-only's solid one.

$enums.$comment: Vocabularies a categorical colour mode can be declared over. A mode bound to an enum MUST colour every member — that is how a member cannot be silently forgotten (doc 10 ⑨/㉜). `water_status` is @app/core `WATER_STATUSES` — the day's status from the status index (`statusIndex.ts`).

$naming: Token names leak into UI copy, so they must not assert anything false. These two were `water.regulated` / `water.other`, which implied some BC water is UNREGULATED. None is: every stream and lake is covered by the general rules for its region and Management Unit. The real distinction is whether WE hold a water-specific record — 2.4% do, 97.6% do not — so the names now describe OUR COVERAGE, not legal status. A toast reading 'no rules held for this water' teaches the single most dangerous inference this app can teach; 'no rules specific to this water — the general rules below apply' does not.
$flow: color.flow.f1..f7 is ONE ramp in seven steps, low-for-the-date to high, and its stops sit at the PERCENTILES they describe (0/10/25/50/75/90/100) rather than at even sixths — 'normal' is the middle half of the record, so half the scale belongs to it. The midpoint is a saturated teal and every stop is mid-dark ON PURPOSE: the previous ramp ran through a sandy beige (#C9BD9A) that was a shade off the map's own paper (#F8F8F2), so the middle of the scale — where most rivers sit most of the time — was invisible over the basemap. A ramp for a MAP cannot pass through the ground's own colour. Teal rather than green so it stays ΔE-distinct from status.open, which means something else entirely.
$aliases: A theme value may NAME another token instead of repeating its hex: "@color.ui.ink". Use it when two tokens are the same colour BY DESIGN (the shadow is the ink; the first donor is the live feed) — the duplicate guard then knows it is one colour on purpose rather than two meanings colliding. `pnpm style:build` resolves it, so the generated themes carry plain values.
$change: color.change.fall2..rise2 is the EXPECTED CHANGE ramp (T52): diverging, a big fall (a quarter of today's flow) through steady to a big rise (four times), its stops at 200 + 100 x the coded ratio in the `standing` channel (@app/core `codedChange`, @app/ui `toRamp`), a domain no percentile reaches. NOT A STATUS COLOUR and not the flow ramp's red-to-blue: light runs green (falling) to violet (rising) and colour-blind green to magenta; dark runs olive to teal, because dark's statuses hold mint, rose and lavender. Never the selection's hue: a tapped river is ringed in `color.highlight` over its own Change colour (light magenta, so light's rise is violet; T52 review). Steady is a tinted grey, a reading and never the ungauged grey (plain greys sit on the boundary edges). Searched to the floors tools/change-colours.test.ts holds, inside the build's own dE76 12 against everything drawn with it.
